title: Spain's Housing Crisis and Inflation Challenge Overshadow Strong Growth Ahead… · 20 Oct
keywords: Spain, housing crisis, inflation, GDP growth, rent controls, housing supply, Spanish election, Banco de España, affordability, fiscal credibility, EU economy, cost of living
notes: Spain faces a deepening affordability crisis as house prices surged 12.2 percent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while inflation projections have risen sharply, complicating the government's economic narrative. With an election approaching, the central question is no longer simply whether Spain is growing, but whether that growth is reaching ordinary households. The contest has become a referendum on whether political instability can deliver stable public finances, lower prices, and homes that citizens can afford.
